TQ2: Demonstrated ability to formulate and implement policy across a geographically dispersed service organization, and to work complex and sensitive issues with other external groups such as other agencies and regulatory bodies. ECQ 2. Driving Efficiency: Demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades. ECQ 3. Merit and Competence: Demonstrated knowledge, ability, and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality. ECQ 4. Leading People: Demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable. ECQ 5. Achieving Results: Demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. The individual must possess a broad point of view and an awareness and understanding of individual or organizational responsibilities in relation to DoW or government-wide strategic priorities. Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is to fly, fight and win...airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Reach and Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do.
MajorDuties: As the Assistant Surgeon General for Personnel and Resources, the incumbent is a key leader responsible for directing and coordinating strategic plans, execution, and decision-making for the Air Force Medical Service's (AFMS) future concepts and capabilities. This role involves driving strategic engagement on Military Health System (MHS) development, overseeing readiness and healthcare programs, and advising senior Air Force, Space Force, and Department of Defense leaders on the health of all personnel and beneficiaries. The position provides oversight for personnel plans, resourcing policies, and the strategic planning and budgeting processes, representing AFMS interests at executive-level boards and councils. Furthermore, the incumbent shares responsibility for the executive leadership and management of the AF/SG staff and Directorates, ensuring the establishment and maintenance of high professional and technical standards. This executive provides direction over a global organization, ensuring mission requirements are met through the integration of activities that have inter-agency, international, and domestic impacts.
Details.Education: Education: A bachelor's degree from an accredited institution is desired. A master's or advanced degree in Healthcare or Business Administration or related fields such as Public Administration or Strategy is highly desired.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.PositionTitle: Senior Technical Leader - Associate General Counsel for Technology Law
MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: The applicant must be a graduate of an accredited law school. In addition, the applicant must be able to demonstrate prior to appointment that he/she is permitted to engage in the active practice of law in the bar of the highest court of a State, U.S. Commonwealth, U.S. Territory, or the District of Columbia. Active status must be maintained in at least one state or other jurisdiction during the course of employment. The applicant must have broad legal experience and professional knowledge of statutes and regulations governing the Intelligence Community. The applicant must also have demonstrated the ability to perform complex legal analysis and give effective oral and written presentations; the ability to forge working relationships with senior-level clients; the ability to effectively manage attorneys; and substantive knowledge and experience with DoD policies and procedures. Ideal candidates will have demonstrated experience as a technical legal expert in one or more of the following areas: technology transfer, CIO authorities, and operational law (e.g., application of DoD Manual 5240.01 and the SIGINT Annex to authorized intelligence activities). Evaluation Criteria: Applicants must meet all the Technical Qualifications (TQs). Applicants must submit a resume, no longer than two pages, reflecting demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and TQs. If your resume exceeds two pages or does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the TQs, you may not receive further consideration for the position. Fully qualified applicants will be reviewed by a Panel. For current DISES, you must submit a copy of your most recent SF-50 in addition to your resume. For all non-DISL applicants, in addition to your resume, you must submit a 3-page document (no less than 11-point font, 1-inch margins) showing evidence that you meet the Executive Core Qualifications described in this Posting. Failure to submit either an SF-50 or your 3-page Executive Core Qualification write-up will disqualify you from consideration.

Details.JobSummary: This position is located in the Office of General Counsel (OGC) of the National Security Agency. NSA is a component of the Department of War (DoW) and NSA/OGC is part of the Defense Legal Service Agency. The General Counsel (GC) of the DoW serves as the chief legal officer of DOW. The DOW GC is also dual-hatted as the Director of DLSA, which provides a full range of legal services to the Office of the Secretary of War, the Defense Agencies, and DoW Field Activities.
MajorDuties: (U) Specific Duties: a) In support of the NSA GC, NSA PDGC, and NSA Deputy GC, provide advice and guidance to senior officials within NSA, to include DIRNSA, regarding the matters described above. b) Interpret all statutes, Presidential Directives, and Executive Branch regulations related to artificial intelligence, emerging technologies, and cybersecurity and provide legal advice and counsel to the Director and Senior Leadership Team, as directed by the NSA GC or NSA PDGC, with respect to the authorities for NSA activities and conditions and restrictions thereon. c) Advise on all matters related to NSA's cybersecurity mission to include responsibilities that arise under National Security Presidential Memorandum-12 and applicable laws and policy directives. d) Provide dynamic support to the OGC Front Office and across OGC practice groups as part of the leadership team responsible for supervising and mentoring a staff of multiple attorneys and unit chiefs; ensuring they are appropriately challenged, rewarded, and given support and tools necessary to succeed. e) Represent the Agency in interactions with the Department of Justice, Department of War, Office of the Director of National Intelligence, Central Intelligence Agency, Federal Bureau of Investigation, Department of Homeland Security, Congress, other government agencies, foreign partners, and the general public. f) Confer with and educate clients, customers, or stakeholders on legal and policy issues. g) Determine legal sufficiency of documents. h) Make legal determinations in accordance with laws, regulations, professional standards, and NSA/CSS policies and procedures. i) Build partnerships with the public and private sectors and within the national security community to advance mission objectives. j) Perform such other duties as the NSA OGC GC, PDGC, or DGC may prescribe.
Details.Evaluations: TECHNICAL QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs): All new entrants into the Defense Intelligence Senior Level (DISL) under a career appointment will be assessed for technical competency against the following mandatory TQs. 1. Technical/Professional Achievements: Specific Technical/Professional Achievement focuses on personal technical achievement, which demonstrates innovative research and/or breakthrough successes. While achievement may take the form of participation in group efforts, the candidate under review should be distinguished from the accomplishments of the team as a whole and evaluated in terms of the impact of individual skills and knowledge on the team effort. 2. Technical/Professional Development of Others: Focuses on supporting and encouraging the development of knowledge, skills and behaviors to enable the next generation of experts to reach their full potential. Covered in this category are not only concrete skills and knowledge, but also such intangibles as how to approach problems, how to balance risk against the chance of success, factors in building problem-solving teams, how to communicate effectively, and the like. Developing skills in others can be accomplished in a multitude of ways beyond mentoring, including but not limited to: building curricula, teaching, or transferring knowledge through papers and talks. 3. Technical Professional Leadership/Decision Making: Demonstrates development as a technical leader to include expertise in logical reasoning, problem solving and emotional intelligence. In this area also fall intangible components of leadership such as integrity, perseverance and dependability. 4. Continued Technical/Professional Development: Focuses on the continuous enhancement of technical/professional skills and knowledge, to include technical leadership skills. Formal training, 'stretch' assignments, research and writing projects, interaction with other experts, and other activities appropriate to the particular discipline should be evaluated as part of the appraisal process. 5. Leading the Intelligence Enterprise: Demonstrates a broad point of view on the intelligence mission and an understanding of individual or organizational responsibilities in relation to the larger Intelligence Community strategic priorities. Aspirant's perspective is shaped by experience and education, and characterized by a strategic, top-level focus on broad requirements, joint experiences, fusion of information, collaboration, and vertical and horizontal integration of information.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is to fly, fight and win...airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Reach and Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do.
MajorDuties: The Technical Advisor serves as a nationally and internationally recognized USAF authority responsible for steering advanced cybersecurity technologies, providing high-level strategic counsel, leading scientific evaluations, and engineering risk-mitigated technical solutions for complex weapon systems and command and control architectures. In this capacity, the advisor operates as the Air Force's foremost technical authority on advanced cybersecurity technologies and their application to weapon systems, networks, and software-defined C4I architectures. The role requires maintaining state-of-the-art expertise in modern enterprise architecture engineering practices, agile software methodologies, open data architectures, artificial intelligence, machine learning, and big data analytics. To shape the future of the field and influence the broader national security landscape, the expert actively produces and presents technical papers and lectures at national and international forums. As a trusted consultant, the advisor delivers critical engineering and computer science guidance to senior leadership across the military and federal government, including the AFLCMC/EN-EZ Director, program directors, HQ AFMC, HQ USAF, and Portfolio Acquisition Executives. This advisory footprint extends externally to industry, academia, Federally Funded Research and Development Centers (FFRDCs), and international allies. The advisor regularly represents USAF interests in executive-level technical coalitions, ensuring that complex policies, processes, and engineering procedures align with defense objectives and state-of-the-art standards. Operating as a scientific catalyst, the advisor leads the Air Force in identifying and exploiting dual-use technologies to enhance C4I system capabilities. This involves initiating and recommending novel scientific studies, research programs, and technical reviews for both Air Force and Space Force projects. The advisor evaluates high-level engineering approaches and possesses the authority to recommend pivotal changes to program directions, statements of objectives, and operational capability requirements documents to maintain technological superiority. The advisor is responsible for driving creative technological solutions into operational weapon systems while aggressively mitigating advanced adversarial cyber threats. By developing comprehensive risk-reduction strategies, the advisor ensures seamless C4I integration, interoperability, and secure netcentric operations. Crucially, the role focuses on proactively countering the exponential security risks introduced by rapid advancements in machine learning, computing power, and modern dual-use technologies across a program's entire lifecycle.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Candidates should be committed to improving the efficiency of the Federal government, passionate about the ideals of our American republic, and committed to upholding the rule of law and the United States Constitution. Candidates will not be hired based on their race, sex, color, religion, or national origin. To meet the minimum qualification requirements for this position, you must show that you possess the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQ) and Technical Qualifications (TQ) related to this position within your resume - NOT TO EXCEED 2 PAGES. Resumes over the 2-page limit, will not be reviewed beyond page 2 or may be disqualified. Your resume should include examples of experience, education, and accomplishments applicable to the qualification(s). If your resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of these qualifications, you may not receive consideration for the position. Separate narratives will not be accepted or reviewed. TECHNICAL QUALIFICATIONS (TQs): Your resume should demonstrate accomplishments that would satisfy the technical qualifications. TQ 1. Extensive experience in planning, designing and executing policy and processes in support of supply chain and related services and associated measurement systems to determine successful performance. TQ 2. Current knowledge of and experience supporting acquisition lifecycle sustainment planning to include exploitation of sustainment planning opportunities in early milestone development. TQ 3. Extensive experience in developing and managing logistics support systems and managing a range of information technology and information system functions. EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs): In addition to the Technical Qualification Requirements listed above, all new entrants into the Senior Executive Service (SES) under a career appointment will be assessed for executive competency against the following five mandatory ECQs. If your 2-page resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and TQs, you may not receive further consideration for the position. ECQ 1: Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding - This core qualification requires a demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people. ECQ 2: Driving Efficiency - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades. ECQ 3: Merit and Competence - This core qualification involves the demonstrated knowledge, ability and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality. ECQ 4: Leading People - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable. ECQ 5: Achieving Results - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. Note: If you are a member of the SES or have been certified through successful participation in an OPM approved SES Candidate Development Program (SESCDP), or have SES reinstatement eligibility, you do not need to respond to the ECQs. Instead, you should attach proof (e.g., SF-50, Certification by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board (QRB)) of your eligibility for noncompetitive appointment to the SES. This is a Critical Acquisition Position (CAP), as defined by the Defense Acquisition Workforce Improvement Act (DAWIA) that has a significant level of responsibility to the success of major acquisition programs. A three-year tenure agreement is required, based upon the position. Additionally, in accordance with DON policy the incumbent must meet the requirements cited below, unless a waiver is granted by the DON Senior Acquisition Executive (SAE) designated approving official: a. Advanced certification in Life Cycle Logistics Career Field, Acquisition Position Category (L) within 48 months of assignment to the position. b. 10 years acquisition experience in an AWF position, at least 4 years of which was performed while assigned to a CAP. c. Other special statutory requirements as applicable to the position. d. A minimum of 80 Continuous Learning points must be earned every two years. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management website: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/senior-executive-service/

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as Director for Supply Chain Performance and Integration, Naval Supply Systems Command (NAVSUP) lead expert in supply chain policy and performance. Authoritative expert and advisor to COMNAVSUP on Navy supply chain performance, technology employment, and systems integration. Provides senior leadership and oversight to subordinate commands, including Weapon Systems Support and regional FLCs.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will provide leadership, direction, and oversight as chief proponent for supply chain management and related services, including inventory, ILS, warehousing, IT, distribution, and cybersecurity, to directly enable Navy readiness.

You will set the enterprise supply chain vision and management philosophy for NAVSUP, continuously assess strategies, goals, and performance; redirect efforts and resources to ensure alignment with Navy objectives and the Commander's intent.

You will serve as the enterprise focal point for NAVSUP supply chain accountability and visibility. Maintain an enterprise-wide program supporting the Commander to ensure compliance with all DoW and DON requirements in this critical area.
You will direct formulation of policies, plans and procedures to evaluate execution of the command's supply chain performance.
You will represent NAVSUP's supply chain management and related services interests at the office of CNO, SECNAV and SECWAR as required as the lead in Navy ERP Program.

You will provide policy and direction for spending over $30B across the FYDP on spares and repairs for aviation, surface, and subsurface readiness. Hold oversight responsibility for a $32B Navy material inventory.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. This position is in the Senior Executive Service (SES) which is a small elite group of top government leaders. SES members possess a diverse portfolio of experiences including strong skills to lead across organizations. As a Senior Executive, you will influence the direction of innovation and transformation of the federal government and lead the next generation of public servants. The Department of the Army is an Equal Opportunity Employer.
MajorDuties: As the Deputy General Counsel (Installations, Energy, and Environment), acts for, assists, and serves in discharging all the responsibilities of the General Counsel and the Principal Deputy General Counsel pertaining to Installations, Energy, and Environmental law matters. Advises the Assistant Secretary of the Army (Installations, Energy and Environment) (IE&E), and Deputy Assistant Secretaries of the Army (IE&E) and staff on issues of policy, programming, and oversight of the Secretary of the Army's responsibilities in the areas of real property, military construction, engineering, housing, base realignment and closures, strategic basing, and compliance with environmental laws. Issues regularly involve relations between the Army and other federal agencies, state and local government, as well as private citizens. Renders advice concerning the relationship between the executive and legislative branches, and other intra-governmental matters arising from the Army's dealing with other federal and state agencies. Participates in the formulation of policy concerning Army programs. Drafts and interprets legislation and identifies legal problems. Performs legal reviews of documents and extensive research of the legislative histories and relevant case law, and prepares legal opinions providing answers, solutions and advice concerning military construction, engineering, real property management and disposal, housing, base realignment and closures, strategic basing, and environmental matters, including environmental restoration. Provides support to the General Counsel, the Principal Deputy General Counsel, and the Senior Deputy General Counsel for Installations, Environment, and Civil Works in the presentation of Army positions before Congress, Office of Management and Budget, Environmental Protection Agency, Department of Justice, other federal agencies, and in negotiations of environmental issues with state and local government agencies. Serves under the general direction of the Senior Deputy General Counsel of the Army for Installations, Environment, and Civil Works. Guidance is received in terms of broad plans, policies, and programs of the Department of the Army. Supervises Installations, Energy and Environment attorneys within the Office of the General Counsel's IECW practice group and provides guidance to Army attorneys engaged in practice of MILCON, housing, real property acquisition and disposal, and environmental restoration and general laws.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Candidates should be committed to improving the efficiency of the Federal government, passionate about the ideals of our American republic, and committed to upholding the rule of law and the United States Constitution. Candidates will not be hired based on their race, sex, color, religion, or national origin. To meet the minimum qualification requirements for this position, you must show that you possess the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQ), and Technical Qualifications (TQ) related to this position within your resume - NOT TO EXCEED 2 PAGES. Resumes over the 2-page limit will be disqualified. Please see "Required Documents" section below for all resume formatting requirements. Your resume should include examples of experience, education, and accomplishments applicable to the qualification(s). If your resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of these qualifications, you may not receive consideration for the position. Do NOT submit a separate narrative statement specifically addressing the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs) or the Technical Qualifications (TQs). TECHNICAL QUALIFICATIONS (TQs): Your resume should demonstrate accomplishments that would satisfy the technical qualifications: TQ 1: Extensive knowledge and experience leading and managing cybersecurity programs, policies, operations, and resources in support of large-scale cybersecurity missions, including cryptographic modernization, identity management solutions, Public Key Infrastructure, Cross Domain Solutions, Key Management Infrastructure, and post-quantum cryptography. TQ 2: Demonstrated knowledge and experience orchestrating the strategic alignment, deployment, and oversight of modernized Cybersecurity and Defensive Cyber Operations, ensuring enterprise-wide readiness and protection of vital critical asset infrastructures. EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs): In addition to the Technical Qualification Requirements listed above, all new entrants into the Senior Executive Service (SES) under a career appointment will be assessed for executive competency against the following five mandatory ECQs. If your 2-page resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and TQs, you may not receive further consideration for the position. There are five ECQs: ECQ 1: Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding - This core qualification requires a demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people. Sub-Competencies: Knowledge of the American System of Government: Demonstrates understanding and appreciation of the American system of government, including the Constitution, the Bill of Rights, separation of powers, federalism, and the historical development of the American Nation. Commitment to the Rule of Law: Upholds the principles of the American Founding, including equality under the law and democratic self-government. Ensures the law is applied fairly and consistently. Civic-Mindedness: Stays up-to-date on important developments in American government and aligns organizational objectives and practices with presidential and public interests. Demonstrates a commitment to serve the American people. ECQ 2: Driving Efficiency - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades. Sub-Competencies: Fiscal Responsibility: Strategically manages, allocates and monitors financial resources. Aligns priorities and initiatives to justify budget proposals. Monitors expenditures, cuts unnecessary costs, and uses cost-benefit analysis to set priorities. Managing Resources: Manages resources efficiently and effectively based on current and projected organizational goals, skills, budget considerations, and staffing needs. Leveraging Technology: Explores emerging technology and potential applications. Incorporates technology to enhance efficiency and achieve results. Ensures access to and security of technology systems. ECQ 3: Merit and Competence - This core qualification involves the demonstrated knowledge, ability and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality. Sub-Competencies: Technical Skill: Possesses the requisite technical knowledge and subject matter expertise to consistently produce timely, high-quality work. Is considered a strong contributor in his or her domain. Problem Solving: Engages in critical and data-driven thinking when diagnosing root causes and evaluating options. Identifies and promptly addresses the most pressing, high-priority problems. Agility and Resilience: Anticipates and adapts to change, new ideas, new information, and new conditions. Is committed to continuous improvement. Deals effectively with pressure and remains optimistic and persistent, even under adversity. ECQ 4: Leading People - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable. Sub-Competencies: Accountability: Ensures that employees are appropriately recruited, selected, appraised, trained, and retained. Takes swift action to address performance- or conduct-based deficiencies in employees supervised. Holds self and others accountable for measurable high-quality, timely, and cost-effective results. Developing Others: Recognizes and rewards outstanding achievement in others. Develops the ability of others to perform and contribute to the organization by providing opportunities to learn through formal and informal methods. Cultivates a dynamic environment in which employees are not afraid to make mistakes. Executive Judgement: Makes well-reasoned, timely, and effective decisions and considers short- and long-term implications. Communicates effectively with stakeholders across all organizational levels, sharing and guarding information where appropriate. ECQ 5: Achieving Results - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. Sub-Competencies: Operational Mindset: Effectively translates strategies into actionable steps and processes. Partners effectively with stakeholders to drive adoption and addresses blockers to ensure successful implementation. Innovation: Applies creativity to improving products and processes, challenges convention, takes measured risks, and considers ways to simplify and remove unnecessary requirements. Strategic Thinking: Formulates objectives and priorities and implements plans consistent with the long-term interests of the organization by evaluating conditions, resources, capabilities, constraints, and organizational goals and values. Note: If you are a member of the SES or have been certified through successful participation in an OPM approved SES Candidate Development Program (SESCDP), or have SES reinstatement eligibility, you must attach proof (e.g., SF-50, Certification by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board (QRB)) of your eligibility for noncompetitive appointment to the SES. See "Required Documents" section for additional information.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: This position is in the Senior Executive Service (SES), a small, elite group of top government leaders. SES members possess a diverse portfolio of experiences including strong skills to lead across organizations. As a Senior Executive, you will influence the direction of innovation and transformation of the federal government and lead the next generation of public servants. The Office of the Secretary of War (OSW) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of War in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSW includes the Offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of War, Under Secretaries of War, Assistant Secretaries of War, General Counsel of the DoW; Director of Cost Assessment and Program Evaluation; Inspector General of the DoW; Director of Operational Test and Evaluation; Chief Information Officer of the DoW; Assistant to the Secretary of War for Public Affairs; Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer; Director of War Innovation; and the Director of Administration and Management.
MajorDuties: Major duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Serves as the Deputy Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) and senior advisor to the Department of War Chief Information Security Officer on Department wide cybersecurity matters. Formulates and executes strategic cybersecurity governance frameworks, policies, procedures, and operational priorities to protect department-wide information systems, networks, and critical infrastructure, while driving decisions that align initiatives with overarching mission capabilities. Provides direction and oversight for implementation of the Cybersecurity Framework functions of Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, and recover across the Department. Ensures cybersecurity efforts are aligned with department mission requirements and national security objectives. Advises the CISO and senior department leaders on significant cybersecurity risks, vulnerabilities, and emerging threats. Recommends actions to address identified risks while balancing cybersecurity requirements with operational and mission needs. Provides strategic direction and oversight for Defensive Cyber Operations and related cybersecurity activities. Assesses Department-wide requirements, establishes priorities, and recommends priorities and actions to improve cyber readiness and resilience. Evaluates the effectiveness of cybersecurity programs, policies, and initiatives and recommends changes based on the performance, mission requirements, emerging threats, and Department priorities. Supports the CISO with oversight for National Security Agency (NSA) Cybersecurity Directorate's execution of the NSA Information Systems Security Program Portfolio, including development and delivery of capabilities related to: cryptographic modernization, identity management solutions, including Public Key Infrastructure, Key Management Infrastructure, Cross Domain Solutions, and post-quantum cryptography.

Details.JobSummary: This position reports to the Chief, National Guard Bureau
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The National Guard Bureau serves as a joint activity of the Department of War (under both the Department of the Army and Department of the Air Force). Its primary purposes are: To act as the official channel of communication between the Department of War and the 54 states, territories, and the District of Columbia (the "54"). To ensure the Army National Guard and Air National Guard are properly organized, manned, trained, equipped, and resourced to perform their federal and state missions. To administer federal policies, programs, and resources for the National Guard.
MajorDuties: The Inspector General is the Department of War Component Inspector General for the NGB and serves as the principal advisor to the CNGB (O-10) and the Vice CNGB (O-10) on all assessed matters relating to the discipline, efficiency, economy, morale, training, and readiness of the NG and NGB, and other oversight matters of importance. NGB-IG as a Personal Staff officer to CNGB serves as an information conduit, with advice on strategic issues and general officer matters within the National Guard. The incumbent liaises with persons and organizations outside NGB to include collaboration with the Departments of War, Army, and Air Force, members of Congress and their staff, as well as Governors and The Adjutants General in the Several States. The incumbent is responsible for the organizational vision and all functions of the NGB-IG including planning, formulation, and execution of policies, objectives, and goals. NGB-IG provides senior-level policy and analytical support to the CNGB and Vice CNGB, and Inspector General support to the Directors of the Army and Air National Guard and the NGB Director of Staff. As the functional manager for National Guard Inspector General activities, NGB-IG develops, leads, and implements the organizational vision of the National Guard Inspector General enterprise, incorporating high performance organization concepts to transform individual efforts into highly productive work-teams by integrating leadership, management, technical and team skills, values, and behaviors. The incumbent directs a required permanent staff of 38 military and civilian inspectors general and oversees the work of 54 State Inspectors General (O-6/O-5 military officers), and through them, up to 500+ inspectors general in the Several States. As the key executive for NGB-IG, the incumbent ensures National Guard equities are included in Department of War and the Departments of the Air Force and Army Inspector General programs and policies. NGB-IG serves as a member of the Defense Council on Integrity and Efficiency and represents National Guard equities at the Department of War Whistleblower Reprisal roundtable and other Departmental working groups. The incumbent is responsible for the execution of Department of War Inspector General programs and activities within the National Guard Bureau, and oversight and execution of the Army and Air Force Inspector General functions for the National Guard, including Army Inspections, Investigations, Assistance, Teach and Train, and Air Force Complaints Resolution and Inspections. This includes oversight of inspections, readiness assessments, sensitive matters, and Department of War, Army and Air Force Senior Official Investigation notifications to the Governors and the CNGB. On behalf of CNGB, NGB-IG also oversees intelligence and intelligence-related oversight responsibilities including the conduct of intelligence oversight inspections throughout the National Guard-assessing the compliance of all activities, operations, and programs with applicable laws, executive orders, policies, and directives. Additionally, NGB-IG is the conduit from the National Guard to the Department of War for reports of Questionable Intelligence Activities and Sensitive/ Highly Sensitive Matters.

Inherent to this senior officer qualification is a deep understanding of the Intelligence enterprise and a shared commitment to the IC's core values. TQ2: Tactical Spectrum Operations. Experience in requirements development and operational implementation of Spectrum capabilities to include Electronic Warfare and Spectrum management. Have deep understanding of the underlying requirements, capabilities and operator training; and of critical threat drivers in the spectrum. TQ3: Space based Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) and Countermeasures. Possess understanding of space based ISR fundamentals and technology drivers. Experience planning and executing multi-domain Counter-Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Cyber, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (C5ISR) operations. ECQ 2: Driving Efficiency - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades. ECQ 3: Merit and Competence - This core qualification involves the demonstrated knowledge, ability and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality. Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is to fly, fight and win...airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Reach and Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do.
MajorDuties: The Director is responsible for the comprehensive development and execution of the Department of the Air Force (DAF) Enterprise Modeling & Simulation (M&S) strategy. The incumbent will review and update the M&S strategy for an enterprise-wide ecosystem while overseeing policy, defining key roles, and managing DAF participation in M&S forums and publications. The Director will develop and manage policy to create a formal M&S Certification process. This duty ensures that M&S-related systems, devices, and programs are compliant with established policies and that development efforts leverage existing products and standards. This is a critical mechanism for enforcing best practices and architectural principles in collaboration with the DAF M&S Steering Committee. The Director monitors, analyzes, and manages current and planned M&S investments across the DAF to identify opportunities for increased capability, return-on-investment, and mission effectiveness. The Director will assess M&S lifecycle costs and value, while also monitoring global M&S technology trends and best practices within the DoW to inform + SecAF about Modeling and Simulation Investments.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Candidates should be committed to improving the efficiency of the Federal Government, passionate about the ideals of our American republic, and committed to upholding the rule of law and the United States Constitution. Candidates will not be hired based on their race, sex, color, religion, or national origin. To meet the minimum qualification requirements for this position, you must show that you possess the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQ) and Technical Qualifications (TQ) related to this position within your resume. Your Resume must be 2 pages. If you submit a resume that exceeds the two-page limit, you will immediately be deemed ineligible for this position and will receive no further consideration. We recommend using a sans-serif font such as Lato, if available. Other acceptable options include Calibri, Helvetica, Arial, Verdana, Open Sans, Source Sans Pro, Roboto, or Noto Sans. Please use 0.5-inch margins. For formatting, consider using a 14-point font for titles and a 10-point font for the main body text. Your resume should include examples of experience, education, and accomplishments applicable to the qualification(s). If your resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of these qualifications, you may not receive consideration for the position. There is NO requirement to prepare a separate narrative statement specifically addressing the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs) or the Technical Qualification (TQ). TECHNICAL QUALIFICATION (TQ): Your resume should demonstrate accomplishments that would satisfy the following technical qualification. TQ: Demonstrated executive-level legal experience and expert legal leadership in advising senior-level officials on civil works regulatory programs, environmental law, and natural resources management. EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs): In addition to the Technical Qualification Requirements listed above, all new entrants into the Senior Executive Service (SES) under a career appointment will be assessed for executive competency against the following five mandatory ECQs. If your 2-page resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and TQ, you may not receive further consideration for the position. There are five ECQs: ECQ 1: Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding - This core qualification requires a demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people. ECQ 2: Driving Efficiency - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades. ECQ 3: Merit and Competence - This core qualification involves the demonstrated knowledge, ability and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality. ECQ 4: Leading People - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable. ECQ 5: Achieving Results - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. Note: If you are a member of the SES or have been certified through successful participation in an OPM approved SES Candidate Development Program (SESCDP), or have SES reinstatement eligibility, you do not need to respond to the ECQs. Instead, you should attach proof (e.g., SF-50, Certification by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board (QRB)) of your eligibility for noncompetitive appointment to the SES.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. This position is in the Senior Executive Service (SES) which is a small elite group of top government leaders. SES members possess a diverse portfolio of experiences including strong skills to lead across organizations. As a Senior Executive, you will influence the direction of innovation and transformation of the federal government and lead the next generation of public servants. The Department of the Army is an Equal Opportunity Employer.
MajorDuties: As the Deputy General Counsel (Civil Works), acts for, assists, and serves in discharging all the responsibilities of the General Counsel, Principal Deputy General Counsel, and the Senior Deputy General Counsel for Installations, Environment, and Civil Works pertaining to the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and civil works program which includes navigation, flood and storm damage reduction projects, Clean Water Act regulatory program; the acquisition, management, and disposal of civil works lands and national resources; and the overall protection of the environment. Advises the Assistant Secretary of the Army (Civil Works), and the Deputy Assistant Secretaries of the Army for Civil Works and their staffs on issues of national and international significance concerning the use and development of the nation's navigable waters, management of civil works lands and other resources, and the overall compliance with environmental laws. Issues regularly involve relations between the Army and other federal agencies, state and local government, as well as private citizens. Renders advice concerning the relationship between the executive and legislative branches, and other intra-governmental matters arising from the Army's dealing with other federal and state agencies. Participates in the formulation of policy concerning Army civil works programs; drafts and interprets legislation and identifies legal problems. Performs legal reviews of documents and extensive research into legislative histories and relevant case law; and prepares legal opinions providing answers, solutions and advice concerning civil works, national resources, real property, and related environmental matters. Provides support to the General Counsel, the Principal Deputy General Counsel, and the Senior Deputy General Counsel for Installations, Environment, and Civil Works in the presentation of Army positions before Congress, Office of Management and Budget, Environmental Protection Agency, Department of Justice, other federal agencies, and in negotiations on civil works, national resources, and environmental issues with state and local government agencies. Serves under the general direction of the Senior Deputy General Counsel for Installations, Environment, and Civil Works. Guidance is received in terms of broad plans, policies, and programs of the Department of the Army. Supervises Office of the General Counsel attorneys supporting the civil works mission.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as the Director of Contracts for Industrial Operations, located in the Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Industrial Operations (PAE IO). As Director, you will have prime responsibility for the management and operation of the PAE IO Contracts Directorate. PAE IO is the single accountable office for maintenance execution and Fleet technical support reporting directly to Assistant Secretary of the Navy for Research, Development and Acquisition (ASN RD&A).
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of PAE IO is to improve fleet readiness and deliver capabilities to our Sailors and Marines with greater speed and agility. The PAE IO reports directly to Assistant Secretary of the Navy for Research, Development and Acquisition (ASN RD&A) for all acquisition and sustainment matters, and accountable to the Chief of Naval Operations (CNO) for all industrial operational requirements and priorities, including the four public Naval Shipyards (NSY) and all Navy Regional Maintenance Centers (RMC). The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will oversee the planning and execution of contracts for the nation's Industrial Operations.
You will originate and promulgate procurement policy for the PAE.
You will counsel and advise the Commander and higher officials on contracting and contracts administration matters as the PAE’s senior civilian procurement executive.
You will supervise the examination, processing and settlement of contractor claims arising under the PAE’s contracts.
You will develop, formulate, and establish policy applicable to the organization.
You will develop procedures for procurement planning, processing of procurement documents timely, dissemination of procurement information, and effective contract negotiation and administration.
You will direct and supervise the overall work of the organization in the planning, negotiation or formal advertising, and administration of the procurements within your cognizance.
You will routinely resolve issues with variances from normal contracting policy, and approval requests for authority to contract.
You will determine course of action when a requirement is changed after proposals are solicited and received with no award made, and evaluate counter proposal of contractor to settle disputes.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Candidates should be committed to improving the efficiency of the Federal government, passionate about the ideals of our American republic, and committed to upholding the rule of law and the United States Constitution. Candidates will not be hired based on their race, sex, color, religion, or national origin. In addition to the minimum qualifications listed below, applicants must demonstrate experience and competency in the Technical Qualifications and Executive Core Qualifications related to this position within your resume - NOT TO EXCEED 2 PAGES. Resumes over the 2-page limit will be disqualified. Your resume should include examples of experience, education, and accomplishments applicable to the qualification(s). If your resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of these qualifications, you may not receive consideration for the position. Separate narratives will not be accepted or reviewed. TECHNICAL QUALIFICATIONS (TQs): Your resume should demonstrate accomplishments that would satisfy the technical qualifications. TQ 1. Knowledge of project development, infrastructure life-cycle management and planning, installation planning, land use, site development, environmental compliance, facilities design and construction critical processes, utilities planning, communication infrastructure planning/design, anti-terrorism/force protection requirements, historic preservation requirements and community interface/interaction management techniques/tools. TQ 2. Knowledge or experience in Federal and DoW acquisition, life cycle management, and energy policy, mandates and goals. Demonstrated expertise in the Planning, Programming and Budgeting System and related budget development and program management for the full lifecycle of infrastructure programs. EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs): In addition to the Technical Qualification Requirements listed above, all new entrants into the Senior Executive Service (SES) under a career appointment will be assessed for executive competency against the following five mandatory ECQs. If your 2-page resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and TQs, you may not receive further consideration for the position. ECQ 1: Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding - This core qualification requires a demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people. ECQ 2: Driving Efficiency - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades. ECQ 3: Merit and Competence - This core qualification involves the demonstrated knowledge, ability and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality. ECQ 4: Leading People - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable. ECQ 5: Achieving Results - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. Note: If you are a member of the SES or have been certified through successful participation in an OPM approved SES Candidate Development Program (SESCDP), or have SES reinstatement eligibility, you do not need to respond to the ECQs. Instead, you should attach proof (e.g., SF-50, Certification by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board (QRB)) of your eligibility for noncompetitive appointment to the SES. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. This is a Key Leadership Position (KLP), as defined by the Defense Acquisition Workforce Improvement Act (DAWIA) that has a significant level of responsibility to the success of major acquisition programs. KLPs receive special attention with regard to qualifications and accountability. Additionally, in accordance with DON policy, the incumbent must meet requirements cited below, unless a waiver* is granted by the DON Senior AcquisitionExecutive (SAE) designated approving official: Certified in the Program Management Functional Area at the Advanced Tier 10 years acquisition experience in an Acquisition Workforce position, at least 4 years of which was performed while assigned to a Critical Acquisition Position Served as Program Manager (PM) or Deputy PM. Complete program manager's course at the Defense Systems Management College (PMT 4010 & PMT 4020) within 6 months of tenure start date. Other special statutory requirements as applicable to the position. A minimum of 80 Continuous Learning points must be earned every two years. *Waivers do not remove a position requirement and shall not exceed 24 months in length. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management website: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/senior-executive-service/

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as Program Management Officer for Construction (PMO Construction) within Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) HQ, located at the Washington Navy Yard.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will enforce Department of the Navy (DON) policy while interpreting and implementing DoW, OMB, and other federal guidance.

You will develop strategic plans, goals, and policies to achieve missions efficiently. Determines and acquires required resources. Establishes execution procedures aligned with organizational priorities, Navy, DoD objectives, and readiness.

You will balance cost, schedule, and performance to field capabilities faster. Directs programming, leads trade councils, integrates operations with acquisitions for requirement trade-offs, and waives technical and certification standards.

You will represent DON construction with industry consortia to share Navy needs and adopt innovation. Builds workforce pipelines via training, talent exchanges, and experiential curricula to scale advanced production capabilities.

You will provide executive direction for acquisition strategies, cost estimates, and schedules. Aligns plans with Navy and DoD objectives. Oversees MILCON programs and coordinates with DON stakeholders to deliver critical infrastructure solutions.
You will review and evaluate program plans, schedules, system engineering efforts, and acquisition strategies, assessing technical, resource, and schedule risks.
You will direct resource estimates, formulations, and funding justifications. Represents MILCON programs before SECNAV, DoW, and Congress to defend resource requirements and expenditure plans.
